rationale: I read the complete held EO 11209 (30 FR 3929, signed March 25, 1965): it establishes the Federal Development Committee for Appalachia and prescribes arrangements for Federal coordination with the Appalachian Regional Commission under the Appalachian Regional Development Act of 1965. It has no own term; its TERM leads are functions, not deadlines. I read the held full text of EO 11386 (33 FR 5, signed December 28, 1967): sec. 9(b) provides 'The Federal Development Committee for Appalachia, established by Executive Order No. 11209 of March 25, 1965, is hereby abolished and that order is hereby revoked.' That names EO 11209 by number and date and revokes the whole order; EO 11386 has no savings clause preserving EO 11209 (its sec. 9(a) amends a different order, EO 11182 on development planning in Alaska). D6 self-check: no held instrument amends EO 11209 between 1965 and 1967. A search of the held full-run texts for '11209' (with OCR spacing variants) finds only EO 11209 itself, EO 11386, and page-number hits in the unrelated EO 9480 and EO 9607 contents columns. Later actions on EO 11386 (partial revocation and revocation) do not name or restore EO 11209, and no revival wording is held. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 11386, December 28, 1967' and the 1989 snapshot row (revoked, actor EO 11386) agree. The machine ACT:EO:11209>EO:11386 pair records come from the APP transcription; I rely on the official FR actor text instead. Both history observations (the API catalog record and the S1989 row) were reviewed; the extra supporting API record is not part of the frozen observation set. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing December 28, 1967, no later effective date stated) is not otherwise adjudicated.
